input: Find founder-owned US specialty chemical distributors with 50-250 employees and no private equity owner

companies.name: Gantrade Corporation
companies.hq: Park Ridge, NJ, USA (founded in Montvale, NJ; the company's July 2025 release is datelined Montvale)
companies.employees: About 62 as of Oct 2026, across North America, Europe and Asia; size band 51-200 (LeadIQ estimate, https://leadiq.com/c/gantrade-corporation/607dbf0a1be80a5a76ceca12)
companies.ownership: founder-owned (inferred: founder Mahendra Parekh is listed as President of a private company; no page I opened shows his share of ownership)

criteria_evidence.evidence: Company release dated July 10, 2025: Gantrade was founded in 1975 in Montvale, NJ by Mahendra Parekh. MarketScreener lists Mahendra Parekh as the current President of Gantrade Corp., described as a private company (no start date or shareholding shown). The Gantrade Europe entities are run by Parekh family members (Hemal Aaron Parekh, Nayan Gregory Parekh).
MarketScreener insider profile: Mahendra Parekh, President, Gantrade Corp. (private company).
Americas office in Park Ridge, NJ, listed first among its offices (others in the UK, Belgium and Dalian, China). LeadIQ also lists the HQ as Park Ridge, New Jersey.

Supplies monomers, intermediates and polymers (polyols, epoxy resins, isocyanates, acrylates, PTMEG, solvents) to coatings, adhesives, sealants and elastomers, plus plastics, construction, textiles and packaging. Stocks inventory on three continents.
About 62 employees as of Oct 2026; size band 51-200 (third-party estimate).

A search for Gantrade acquisitions or private equity deals in 2024-2026 found nothing (results were only namesakes such as Gantrex and Gantner). Neither Gantrade's own pages nor MarketScreener mention an outside investor; MarketScreener lists it as private.

companies.traction: 50th anniversary in 2025, with entities opened in the UK (1981), China (2005) and Belgium (2019). Site headlines mention a Union Pacific Pinnacle Award for the second year running and a North American launch of ROPOL polycarbonate polyols with Cromogenia. LeadIQ estimates revenue at $50M-$100M (as of Oct 2026). Sources: https://www.gantrade.com/blog/gantrade-corporation-celebrates-50-years-of-excellence-innovation-and-global-growth ; https://leadiq.com/c/gantrade-corporation/607dbf0a1be80a5a76ceca12
companies.rank_reason: The only candidate with evidence for every criterion: US-based, distributes CASE and urethane specialty intermediates, about 62 employees, the 1975 founder still listed as President, and no private equity deal found. Two weak points: ownership is inferred from his title rather than from a filing, and the headcount is a third-party estimate near the bottom of the range. Not bootstrapped, so there is no funding round; last_round is null.

output.search_notes: Scope as of 2026-11-10. I read 'founder-owned' strictly as the founder still owning the company. Multi-generation family firms, ESOPs and owners who bought out the founder do not count. Only Gantrade qualified. missing_fields for Gantrade: headcount_growth (I opened only one dated count; a search snippet put LeadIQ at about 69 as of Dec 2025, but I did not open that version, so there are not two verified dated counts) and last_round (no funding round found). EXCLUDED, owned by private equity or a strategic buyer: Mays Chemical (sold to Ravago, July 2024; capstonepartners.com); Shrieve Chemical (Gemspring Capital, continuation vehicle led by StepStone); Connection Chemical (bought by Shrieve, Nov 2024); EMCO Chemical (founder-owned but over 500 employees, and Lindsay Goldberg agreed to buy it; mdm.com); Aakash Chemicals (CenterOak Partners majority stake, 2017); Callahan Chemical (Tilley-Phoenix/SK Capital, 2022); Charkit Chemical (LeBaronBrown Industries majority stake); U.S. Chemicals (Maroon Group/CI Capital, 2016); M.F. Cachat (IMCD, 2015); Ribelin (KODA, then Azelis); Deveraux Specialties (Safic-Alcan, 2026); Access Ingredients (Vivify/Gryphon). EXCLUDED, employee-owned: Sea-Land Chemical (100% ESOP), Essential Ingredients (employee-owned; founders Maynard and Gerlach), Dorsett & Jackson, TCR Industries, Palmer Holland. EXCLUDED, family-owned but the founder no longer owns it: Coyne Chemical (founded 1868), GJ Chemical (now led by Diana Colonna and Robert Masci; LeadIQ about 255 employees), Seeler Industries (founded 1978; Steve Seeler, EVP in 2013 and now CEO, so likely second generation), Lintech International (founder Tom Hinson was succeeded by CEO Julie Van Brunt in 2013; woman-owned), Catalynt Solutions/TRInternational (founder Anthony Ridnell; CEO Megan Gluth bought 100% in 2021). NEAR-MISSES, a criterion could not be verified: Wego Chemical Group, Great Neck NY (founded 1978, privately owned, 'family-built', 200+ employees per womeninchemicals.com, led by CEO Bert Eshaghpour; no source confirms he or a relative founded it, and directories also name partner Edward Khalily); Silver Fern Chemical, Seattle (founded 2004 by Lisa and Sam King, who still run it as a family business with nine US warehouses; headcount unverified, with directories ranging from about 15 to 50-100, and the Vaia listing appeared to describe a Santa Barbara entity); Chem-Materials, Westlake OH (in business since 1987, president Phil Haagensen; founder, ownership and headcount not found). EXCLUDED, too small: The Plaza Group, Houston (founder Randy Velarde; about 35 employees, mainly petrochemical marketing) and Tri-iso (about 11-25 employees). EXCLUDED, other: RSC Chemical Solutions (mainly a manufacturer, not founder-owned) and Norman, Fox & Co. (manufacturer and repackager; ownership unverified). Limits: I could not read two PDFs (a CCD Partners 2025 distribution watchlist and a 2019 Form 5500 filing for Silver Fern), the Alliance for Chemical Distribution full member directory was not opened, and several headcounts come from third-party estimates. Next steps would be the ACD member list, state filings for Wego and Silver Fern, and LinkedIn headcounts.
